title: Essay Writing: Narrative, Descriptive and Argumentative
summary: The writing process and the features of narrative, descriptive and argumentative essays, with paragraphing, openings and the Grade 10 length of 250–300 words.

items: **Plan**: brainstorm or mind-map ideas; decide on purpose and audience.
**Revise**: improve content, structure and word choice.
**Edit and proofread**: correct spelling, grammar and punctuation.
**Final copy**: give it a title and write neatly.

notes.label: Length
notes.text: A Grade 10 Home Language essay is usually **250–300 words**. Show your planning; it is part of the process.

rows: Plot with conflict and climax; characters; dialogue; usually past tense
Sensory details (sight, sound, smell, taste, touch); figurative language; little or no plot
Clear stance in the introduction; reasons with evidence; counter-argument rebutted; strong conclusion
Balanced arguments; conclusion may give a reasoned view
Think about an experience or idea
First person; personal insight and growth

items: Start in the middle of the action: 'The glass shattered before I could scream.'
Use dialogue: '"Don't look down," my brother whispered.'
Ask a question (argumentative): 'Should cellphones be allowed in class?'
Use a vivid image (descriptive): 'The market smelled of cinnamon and diesel.'

notes.text: Each paragraph has one main idea in a **topic sentence**, supported by details. Use **transition words**: 'firstly', 'however', 'as a result', 'meanwhile', 'in conclusion'. In narratives, start a new paragraph for a new speaker, a new time or a new place.

notes.label: Show, don't tell
notes.text: Instead of 'I was nervous', write 'My palms were damp and I read the same line four times.'

questions.prompt: How long should a Grade 10 HL essay usually be?
Which essay type presents BOTH sides of an issue fairly?
Which essay type relies most on sensory details?
What is the sentence that states the main idea of a paragraph called?
In a narrative, you should start a new paragraph when a new character speaks.
Match each stage of the writing process to its activity.
Rewrite to 'show, not tell': 'The room was scary.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ Uses specific sensory detail to create fear, e.g. 'Shadows crawled across the peeling walls and the floorboards groaned beneath my feet.' (2)

questions.prompt: Write an effective opening sentence for a narrative essay titled 'The Storm'.
questions.memo:
✓ Engaging hook (action, dialogue or vivid image) (1)
✓ Linked to the title, correct language (1)

questions.prompt: Why should an argumentative essay mention and rebut a counter-argument?
questions.memo:
✓ It shows the writer has considered other views (1)
✓ and strengthens the argument by showing why the opposing view is weaker (1)

questions.prompt: Plan an argumentative essay on 'School uniforms should be abolished': state your stance and give TWO reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ Clear stance (1)
✓✓ Two relevant, distinct reasons (2)
